title: Optimal CGLMP measurements for a maximally entangled state

source.latex:
Zohren and Gill formulate the standard Fourier-phase measurements as the
candidate global optimizers of the CGLMP value for a fixed maximally entangled
state \sourcecite{ref:p24-zohren-gill}{ZG08}.

progress.latex:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Collins, Gisin, Linden, Massar, and Popescu introduced the
  high-dimensional Bell family and the Fourier--phase measurement
  construction underlying Eq.~\eqref{eq:p24-cglmp-bases}
  \sourcecite{ref:p24-cglmp}{CGLMP02}.

  \item Zohren and Gill explicitly identify optimality of
  Eq.~\eqref{eq:p24-cglmp-bases} for the fixed state in
  Eq.~\eqref{eq:p24-maximally-entangled-state} as a longstanding conjecture
  and provide numerical support.  They do not prove it for arbitrary $d$
  \sourcecite{ref:p24-zohren-gill}{ZG08}.

  \item For $d=3$, Lang, Vértesi, and Navascués obtained a semidefinite upper
  bound on the optimum over maximally entangled states that differs from the
  candidate value by about $10^{-10}$.  This numerical certification is not
  an exact proof and does not address all dimensions
  \sourcecite{ref:p24-lang}{LVN14}.
\end{itemize}

comment.latex:
The unresolved statement is global measurement optimality for every finite
$d$ with the state fixed by Eq.~\eqref{eq:p24-maximally-entangled-state}.  It
does not ask for the unrestricted CGLMP optimum over shared states, which is a
different problem.
